key_insight: The paper turns diffusion models into in-context learners by using a context set to infer a task-specific score function for previously unseen distributions.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid adaptation of generative models to new scientific or visual datasets without retraining, which is useful for simulation, forecasting, and data-driven design workflows.
method: Represent each target distribution as a task specified by context samples at inference time.
Learn an in-context score operator with a transformer that takes context, noisy query, and diffusion time as input.
Use a Gaussian-kernel conditional-mean view and Nadaraya–Watson approximation to justify the query-dependent attention architecture.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on Navier-Stokes, ERA5 climate data, QuickDraw, and Food-101, where it works well on simpler task families.
watch_item: Performance degrades as task complexity increases, so the approach may be sensitive to harder distributions and context quality.
paper_title: Transformer-based In-Context Score Operator Learning for Diffusion Models
